question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 4% per month for 10 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage for 10 months = 4% × 10 = 40%

Simple Interest = 40% of ₹1,200

Simple Interest = (40 ÷ 100) × 1200 = ₹480

**∴ The correct answer is ₹480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,200

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% per month

Time (T) = 10 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Principal
 ₹1,200
 
 
• 
 
 
 4% / month
 for 10 months
 
 
• 
 
 
 Interest
 ₹480

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (1200 × 4 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 40

⇒ SI = ₹480

**∴ The correct answer is ₹480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Consistency in SI Formula

Ensure the Rate (R) and Time (T) are in the same time units before calculating. If R is per month, T must be in months. If R is per annum, T must be in years.

Compound Interest (CI) Formula

Amount = P(1 + R÷100)T. Unlike Simple Interest, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal as well as the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Difference Between SI and CI

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain principal P at rate R is derived using the formula: Difference = P(R÷100)².
